evidence.exact_quote: This document owns the operational migration path from current bootstrap planning files to standardized canonical Plan docs and, later, native Puppet Master planning services. It covers AGENTS trigger rules, Codex phase usage, compact goal prompts, lossless Plan conversion sequencing, governance seal timing, and retired-experiment exclusions.

canonical_text: Root AGENTS.md defines trigger phrases and read/write rules so Codex knows when to start, continue, compile, standardize, index, report readiness, or seal through the PM Bootstrap Planning Ledger workflow.

items.impact: Defines the migration workflow's trigger and authority surface while keeping ledger memory distinct from canonical plan prose.
items.statement: The document establishes an operator-triggered bootstrap migration workflow, and BPM-001 assigns the root AGENTS.md the trigger phrases and read/write routing rules for each phase.
items.title: Bootstrap migration trigger surface

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: Bootstrap use in the Mac Codex app may use separate threads per phase. Conversational ledger creation usually runs in normal chat; compile, audit, migration, indexing, node-readiness, and governance seal phases use Goal Mode. Goal prompts stay compact, with reusable repo files, skills, and context carrying the detail.
- Goal prompts stay less than 4,000 characters when possible by reading repo instructions and compact state.

items.impact: Separates conversational planning from artifact-transforming phases and constrains prompt size to preserve continuity.
items.statement: BPM-002 permits separate Codex threads, keeps conversational ledger updates outside mandatory Goal Mode, and places transformation phases in Goal Mode with compact prompts.
items.title: Codex phase and compact-prompt model

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: The bootstrap design compiles first into Planning_Ledger_System.md, Plan_Document_System.md, Plan_To_Node_Compilation.md, Bootstrap_Planning_Migration.md, and the Plans index registration. This creates owner docs before broader Plan conversion.
- The ledger remains source lineage, not canonical prose.

items.impact: Establishes the initial canonical owner-doc set and routing index before conversion of the wider plan corpus.
items.statement: BPM-003 requires the four canonical owner docs and Plans index registration to exist before broader Plan conversion, while preserving the ledger only as lineage.
items.title: Initial canonical owner-doc compilation

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: Existing Plans convert losslessly through inventory, original hashes, heading/body span maps, coverage maps, ContractRef preservation, anchor or alias preservation, explicit dispositions, a representative pilot conversion, validators, and controlled batches.
- Content deletion or semantic change without source coverage stops the migration.

items.impact: Creates a loss-prevention gate around conversion and makes uncovered deletion or semantic change a stop condition.
items.statement: BPM-004 defines a staged, evidence-backed, lossless conversion contract with inventory, hashes, span and coverage maps, preservation obligations, a pilot, controlled batches, validators, and a hard stop on uncovered change.
items.title: Controlled lossless Plan conversion

evidence.exact_quote: - Content deletion or semantic change without source coverage stops the migration.
- Validators after pilot and each batch.

items.impact: A stopped or partially applied batch can leave canonical documents and conversion evidence out of sync, with no specified resume, rollback, or commit boundary.
items.statement: BPM-004 says when migration must stop but does not define atomic batch boundaries, partial-write detection, rollback or restoration behavior, resumable state, concurrent-editor exclusion, or the oracle that proves a failed batch left canonical Plans unchanged.
items.title: Lossless conversion lacks transactional recovery semantics

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: Spec Lock, generated shards, evidence bundles, plan graph, and governance locks are refreshed only during an explicit governance seal phase after canonical docs and generated indexes stop changing.
- Ordinary ledger writing, plan drafting, plan conversion batches, and PlanUnit indexing do not update Spec Lock or generated governance artifacts.

items.impact: Prevents governance artifacts from being refreshed during ordinary drafting, conversion, and indexing.
items.statement: BPM-005 reserves Spec Lock and generated-governance mutation to an explicit seal phase after canonical documents and generated indexes stabilize.
items.title: Governance seal mutation boundary

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: Spec Lock, generated shards, evidence bundles, plan graph, and governance locks are refreshed only during an explicit governance seal phase after canonical docs and generated indexes stop changing.
- The seal phase runs only after doc/index churn stops.

items.impact: A seal can race new canonical edits or fail midway, producing a mutually inconsistent Spec Lock, shards, evidence, graph, and decision log without a defined recovery path.
items.statement: The seal gate never defines how doc/index stability is detected, who acquires mutation authority, whether inputs are snapshotted or locked, how multi-artifact publication is committed, or how partial refresh failure is rolled back and reported.
items.title: Governance sealing has no stability or atomicity protocol

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: Retired legacy transfer experiments are stale/retired source-lineage only. The replacement architecture is Goal + new ledger + validators + compact operating views. Exact retired labels remain in ledger/source evidence when needed, not in active architecture prose.
- Do not reference retired legacy experiment mechanics as the basis of the new architecture.

items.impact: Blocks stale experimental mechanics from re-entering active architecture while allowing exact historical lineage to remain auditable.
items.statement: BPM-006 explicitly retires legacy transfer experiments as architecture and permits their terms only in stale lineage or negative constraints.
items.title: Retired experiments are lineage only

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: Bootstrap work may run across separate Codex threads. Each phase starts from the relevant ledger_id, compact state, and canonical owner docs; each phase ends by updating handoff/projection state, reporting validators, and leaving an exact next safe action. Conversational ledger creation is not required to use Goal Mode; transformation phases should use compact Goal prompts under the Codex objective limit.
- Every phase produces a clear handoff and validator list before stopping.

items.impact: Provides the minimum continuity contract needed to restart each bootstrap phase in another thread.
items.statement: BPM-007 defines phase entry from ledger identity, compact state, and owner docs, and phase exit through updated handoff/projection state, validator reporting, and an exact next safe action.
items.title: Cross-thread phase handoff contract

evidence.exact_quote: - Every phase produces a clear handoff and validator list before stopping.
- Plans/ledgers/v2/<ledger_id>/state/handoff.json

items.impact: A new thread cannot reliably distinguish complete, current, validated handoff state from stale, malformed, partially written, or mismatched state.
items.statement: BPM-007 names handoff.json and required handoff concepts but does not specify its schema, freshness/version binding, atomic write protocol, validation failure behavior, stale-thread conflict handling, or authentication of the claimed ledger and prior phase.
items.title: Thread handoff lacks integrity and freshness semantics

evidence.exact_quote: The ledger-to-Plans Goal prompt must require many bounded read-only subagents in parallel when atom, owner, or document thresholds are exceeded, require assignment/result evidence, and block rather than silently use one broad agent; main agent remains sole writer.
- main agent is the only writer

items.impact: Defines a parallel read-only review topology with one mutation authority and an explicit block when the required topology cannot be used.
items.statement: BPM-008 requires threshold-triggered parallel bounded read-only agents, assignment/result evidence, and a sole main-agent writer for ledger-to-Plans compilation.
items.title: Mandatory parallel evidence and sole-writer contract

evidence.exact_quote: when atom, owner, or document thresholds are exceeded
- HARD PARALLEL GATE

items.impact: Different operators can trigger or bypass the required parallel topology inconsistently, and no validator can falsify compliance.
items.statement: BPM-008 makes parallelism mandatory above atom, owner, or document thresholds but supplies no numeric thresholds, counting rules, minimum meaning of many, maximum assignment size, capacity exception, or machine-checkable gate oracle.
items.title: Hard parallel gate is not numerically defined

evidence.exact_quote: The repair Goal builds a closure matrix only for repair_required=true findings, repairs or adjudicates those actionable rows, updates the semantic closure registry only for actionable closures, uses bounded read-only specialist subagents, and no-ops when no actionable rows exist.
Passing validators alone are insufficient when repair_required=true rows remain unclosed.

items.impact: Restricts repair work and semantic-closure mutation to actionable findings and prevents green validators from masking unresolved repair obligations.
items.statement: BPM-008 defines repair selection, adjudication, closure-registry mutation, no-op behavior, and the rule that validator success cannot close unresolved repair_required rows.
items.title: Actionable-only repair and closure behavior

evidence.exact_quote: - many bounded read-only subagents in parallel
- main agent is the only writer

items.impact: Agent crashes, duplicate or overlapping assignments, stale results, forged evidence, and incomplete coverage can be merged by the sole writer without a defined rejection or retry rule.
items.statement: The parallel-agent contract does not define assignment identity, result schema, evidence binding, coverage-union checks, duplicate work handling, timeout/retry behavior, cancellation, capacity shortfall behavior, or how the sole writer rejects partial and untrusted results.
items.title: Parallel evidence lacks failure and trust semantics

evidence.exact_quote: Ledger-to-Plans compilation writes or updates canonical Plans and allowed PlanUnit indexes only in their proper phases; it does not start Plan Compile, create WorkNodes, launch GoalRuns, modify implementation code, or start an Orchestrator build.
- Do not confuse the bootstrap compile Goal with the finished-product Approve And Build runtime.

items.impact: Prevents a planning compile from silently escalating into runtime dispatch, implementation, or build execution.
items.statement: BPM-008 confines ledger-to-Plans compilation to canonical Plans and allowed PlanUnit indexes and expressly excludes Plan Compile, WorkNodes, GoalRuns, implementation changes, and Orchestrator builds.
items.title: Ledger compile is not runtime authority

segments.summary: Reviewed all 396 assigned lines and every required PlanUnit and semantic unit. The migration sequencing, sole-writer and non-runtime boundaries, and actionable-only repair rules are explicit; material gaps remain in conversion rollback, seal atomicity, handoff integrity, parallel-gate measurability, multi-agent failure handling, and the document's accepted-versus-lineage-only authority seam.
